title: DROP INDEX
description: Learn how to remove indexes from tables using the DROP INDEX statement.

data.text: The DROP INDEX statement removes one or more indexes from the current database. Use the IF EXISTS option to avoid errors when dropping an index that may not exist.

data.title: DROP INDEX with IF EXISTS
data.content: Safely drops an index if it exists.
data.code:
DROP INDEX [IF EXISTS] index_name
ON table_name;

data.text: Note that the IF EXISTS option has been available since SQL Server 2016 (13.x). The DROP INDEX statement does not remove indexes created by PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraints — use ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT for those.

data.title: Drop one index
data.content: Removes the ix_cust_email index from the customers table.
data.code:
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cust_email
ON sales.customers;

data.title: Drop multiple indexes
data.content: Removes multiple indexes from the same table in one statement.

data.text: What Dropping an Index Costs You

Dropping an unused index frees storage and speeds up writes, but you must be sure nothing relies on it. Use `sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats` to find indexes that have never been used since the last restart before you drop anything.

data.title: Find unused indexes, then drop one
data.content: The usage-stats query is read-only and safe to run in production; the DROP is commented out so you can review first.
data.code:
SELECT
    OBJECT_NAME(i.object_id) AS table_name,
    i.name                  AS index_name,
    us.user_seeks,
    us.user_scans,
    us.user_lookups,
    us.user_updates
FROM sys.indexes AS i
LEFT JOIN sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats AS us
       ON us.object_id = i.object_id AND us.index_id = i.index_id
WHERE i.object_id = OBJECT_ID('sales.customers')
  AND i.type_desc = 'NONCLUSTERED'
ORDER BY us.user_seeks, us.user_scans;

-- Drop an unused index
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cust_city ON sales.customers;

data.title: A dropped clustered index turns the table into a heap
data.text: `DROP INDEX` on a clustered index does not delete the data — it converts the table to a heap, which changes how every non-clustered index locates rows. If an index backs a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint, `DROP INDEX` fails; use `ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT` instead.

data.title: DROP INDEX Key Points
points: Use DROP INDEX to remove non-clustered indexes from tables.
Always use IF EXISTS to avoid errors on non-existent indexes.
DROP INDEX cannot remove indexes created by PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraints.
You can drop multiple indexes in a single DROP INDEX statement.
